svg.text: Casino sign - electrical schematic (Mega 2560 + Grove shield with 11 LED sticks, 3 WS2812B strips)
Grove stick: upper rail, left stick
Grove stick: upper rail, right stick
Grove stick: lower rail, left stick
Grove stick: lower rail, right stick
Grove stick: CLOSED light, behind the plate
arrow direction: handle on the GND side
mount: back view, GND contact on the right
casino closed: handle on the GND side = LOW =
CLOSED (OPEN letters off, CLOSED light on);
handle on the other side = casino open
speed of the frame and the arrow
shows mode, speeds, casino state, arrow
USB-B cable (upload, Serial Monitor): ONLY while the LED supply
is switched OFF. The supply feeds the Mega 5V pins (the sticks
get their power through the Grove shield), so with USB plugged in
as well two 5 V sources would be connected together.
hop = lines cross without a connection; dot = connection
Total: 164 LEDs in 3 WS2812B strips (14 pieces) plus 11 Grove sticks with 10 LEDs each (10 arrow
sticks + the CLOSED light). Positions: layout-diagram.svg, arrow_sticks/.
1. Common ground: PSU V-, Arduino GND (and the shield) and the GND of every LED strip piece and
2. Put each 330 ohm resistor close to the first LED of its strip. Keep data wires short. The sticks
plug straight into the Grove shield (no resistors).
3. Feed +5 V and GND into every strip piece from the buses (thick wire, at least 1 mm2). Where the
diagram says 'start and end', feed the strip at both ends. The DIN end of a strip is the end the
arrow printed on the strip points away from.
4. Strips made of several pieces (frame edges, letter groups) are chained: DOUT of one piece to DIN
of the next, and each piece gets its own +5 V and GND connection.
5. The Mega's 5 V logic drives WS2812B and the sticks directly: no level shifter. Fit F1 right after
6. SW3 and SW4: pins 1, 2, 4, 8 go to D22-D25 and D26-D29, the common pin C goes to GND. A position
counts in binary (0..F). If your switch gives the complement (15 - position), set
7. All inputs (SW1 to SW5) use the internal pull-ups (INPUT_PULLUP), so no resistors are needed for
8. CLOSED (the 11th Grove stick, 10 white LEDs, shield connector A3) sits BEHIND the plate under the
CLOSED hole text and is lit only while SW5 says closed. Like all sticks it is plugged into the
shield: no wire from the supply to it.
9. LCD1 (I2C backpack) uses the Mega's I2C pins D20 (SDA) and D21 (SCL) plus the Mega 5V and GND
10. Arrow sticks: the 10 Grove RGB LED sticks go into the Grove Base Shield connectors D2-D8 and
A0-A2 (A3 carries the CLOSED light stick; the shield's 3V3/5V switch must be on 5 V). Connect
the +5 V bus to BOTH 5V pins of the Mega's long header and the GND bus to the Mega GND pins, as
in stick_test_direct (tested on real hardware). The Mega 5V pin therefore carries the stick
current: keep the brightness curve max moderate.
11. Pin 13 (the LED on the Mega board) blinks while the program runs; the Serial Monitor (115200
baud) shows one line per second.
